name: Sale of Goods Directive
impact_assessment: SWD(2015) 274 (executive summary SWD(2015) 275), joint with the Digital Content Directive
evidence_rating: thin: a 2024 coordinated sweep of 356 online second-hand sellers found 57% not respecting the minimum legal guarantee; the review due June 2024 was not found
summary: The Directive harmonised consumers' rights when goods bought in shops or online are faulty, including a minimum two-year guarantee. The Commission forecast slightly lower prices, 122,000 more firms selling across borders online and about EUR 4 billion a year more GDP. None of this has been measured: the review due in June 2024 has not been found, and the rules have since been amended by the 2024 Right to Repair Directive without an evaluation.

indicators.objective: The proposal's financial statement has no indicators section; the memorandum mentions only transposition monitoring. Article 25 required a review report by 12 June 2024, which was not found published

indicators.type: expected impact (impact assessment, joint with Digital Content)
indicators.indicator: Share of businesses selling online cross-border up by more than 5 percentage points (about 122,000 firms)

indicators.type: expected impact (impact assessment, joint with Digital Content)
indicators.indicator: Retail prices -0.25%; 8-13 million more cross-border online shoppers spending EUR 40 more each a year

indicators.type: expected impact (impact assessment, joint with Digital Content)

indicators.indicator: One-off contract adaptation cost of about EUR 7,000 per firm
Right to Repair Directive (EU) 2024/1799 amends the Directive (12-month extension of seller liability when consumers choose repair)
indicators.evidence: The repair impact assessment reviewed how the remedies work but did not evaluate the Directive's market effects; several Member States said it was too early as the rules had only just applied.

literature.citation: European Commission (2015), Impact Assessment accompanying the proposals for Directives on contracts for the supply of digital content and for online and other distance sales of goods (executive summary SWD(2015) 275), SWD(2015) 274
literature.title: Impact Assessment accompanying the proposals for Directives on contracts for the supply of digital content and for online and other distance sales of goods (executive summary SWD(2015) 275)
literature.method: ex-ante (survey-based estimates and CGE macro model)
literature.headline: Removing contract-law barriers would raise the share of firms selling cross-border online by more than 5 pp (122,000 firms), cut retail prices 0.25%, add 8-13m cross-border shoppers and raise GDP 0.03% (EUR 4bn a year); one-off cost about EUR 7,000 per firm
literature.summary_plain: The Commission expected common EU rules on faulty goods to cut prices slightly, bring more shops and shoppers online across borders and add about EUR 4 billion a year to GDP.
literature.quality: forecast for the original online-only proposal; the adopted Directive covers all sales

literature.citation: European Commission (2023), Impact Assessment Report accompanying the proposal on common rules promoting the repair of goods, SWD(2023) 59
literature.title: Impact Assessment Report accompanying the proposal on common rules promoting the repair of goods
literature.method: ex-ante (with consultation on functioning of Sale of Goods remedies)
literature.headline: Uses the Sale of Goods Directive as the vehicle for repair incentives; notes Member States' concern that it was too early to change rules that had only just applied; no ex-post measurement of the Directive's effect on trade or prices
literature.summary_plain: When proposing a right to repair, the Commission built on these rules but did not measure how they have affected trade or prices.

literature.authors: European Commission and national CPC authorities
literature.title: Sweep on online traders of second-hand goods (2024)
literature.venue: European Commission, consumer protection enforcement: sweeps page
literature.method: coordinated compliance screening (sweep) of 356 online second-hand traders by authorities of 25 Member States, Iceland and Norway
literature.outcomes: compliance with legal guarantee of conformity, withdrawal information and green claims
literature.headline: Of 356 online second-hand traders screened, 57% did not respect the minimum 1-year legal guarantee for second-hand goods and 45% did not correctly inform consumers about the legal guarantee of conformity.
literature.summary_plain: National consumer authorities checked hundreds of websites selling used goods and found that more than half did not honour the minimum one-year guarantee that EU sales law allows for second-hand items.
literature.quality: Compliance snapshot with numbers but non-random targeted sample, no pre/post comparison; covers several directives (SGD, CRD, UCPD); Commission-coordinated.
literature.interested_party: Commission and enforcement authorities reporting on own enforcement
literature.citation: European Commission and national CPC authorities (2024), Sweep on online traders of second-hand goods (2024), European Commission, consumer protection enforcement: sweeps page

evidence_rating_previous: none ex-post: forecasts only; the review due June 2024 was not found and no independent impact studies were found
